criteria.rationale: For deeptech hardware the defining risk is the path to commercial use: accuracy in the field, certification and liability. The founders name accuracy across motor types, hardware supply and sales cycles as risks without being asked. They flag their own value data as unaudited and invite scrutiny of calibration. But they show no plan: no false-alert or missed-failure rates, certifications unnamed despite 25% of the raise, liability absent. Their own figures also do not reconcile on subscription revenue. Scored on behaviour, not credentials (C002 applied on S3).

evidence.text: Key risks named: sensor accuracy across motor types, hardware supply, longer sales cycles in larger plants.
Value evidence flagged by founders as customer-reported, not audited; founders invite a calibration and scale-up conversation and offer pilot data.
Form gives ~INR 0.9 L cumulative non-hardware revenue, while the deck's paid-sensor ramp at INR 750/sensor/month implies ~INR 3 L subscription June-October.
25% of raise for 'Certification and operations' with no certification named; wireless devices generally need WPC ETA.

criteria.rationale: The founders visited 38 plants in two industrial clusters before scaling, then ran 11 hands-on pilots (10 free sensors for 30 days each). They sell through a cluster association and pump distributors. The application does not say what broke in pilots or what they changed.

11 pilots of 10 free sensors for 30 days; 6 converted to paid.

Two things hold it back: the 12-month targets don't add up on the founders' own numbers (INR 12 L MRR needs ~53 sensors per customer, not 23), and inventory plus certification will absorb cash.

gates.detail: Checked all 88 portfolio companies. No company serves MSME factories with machine-health monitoring. Nearest adjacencies: Mowito (AI models for industrial robots: factory customer, different job); Unbox Robotics (warehouse automation); Fleetx (fleet telematics: different asset and customer); Nawgati (fuel-station compliance/ops SaaS); REint (renewable supply prediction); Grid (IoT ODM, a possible supplier, not a competitor). None share both customer and job.
No dependence on a withdrawn or ungranted permission. Radio type approval (WPC ETA) is a standard certification step, scored under R4.
Selected Deeptech, and the business (sensor hardware plus a learning model) genuinely fits it.
Pre-seed, INR 2.2 Cr at INR 11 Cr post-money, grant and angels only. Within the lead mandate.

case_for: Went to the customer: 38 plant visits, then 11 hands-on pilots with a 55% conversion to paid (R2, R3).
Unit economics are clear, and hardware margin funds acquisition. The round fits a pre-seed cheque (R4, R5, S2).
Founders name their own risks and flag their value data as unaudited, which is a good candour signal (R1).
Deeptech and vertical AI built by engineers who designed and shipped the product (S1, S3).
case_against: Revenue is ~94% one-off hardware, and collected subscription (~INR 0.9 L) does not reconcile with the deck's sensor ramp (~INR 3 L implied). This is an inconsistency in the founders' own figures (R1, R3).
No accuracy data (false alerts, missed failures), no named certification path, and no liability position: three deeptech key metrics are missing (R1, R4).
12-month MRR target is inconsistent with the founders' own sensors-per-customer figure (R5).
Well-funded competitor Infinite Uptime and OEM Kirloskar are not addressed; half the customers come from one association (R4, R6, S4).
call_questions: How much subscription has actually been invoiced and collected, month by month? Are any customers on free months, and why is non-hardware revenue only ~INR 0.9 L?
Across 140 sensors, how many alerts fired, how many were confirmed faults, and were any failures missed?
Which certifications do you need before selling to larger plants, what will they cost, and when will you have them?
What do customer contracts say about a motor that fails without an alert, and do you carry liability cover?
The 12-month target of INR 12 L MRR needs ~53 sensors per customer, but you have 23. Which assumption is wrong? (Pressure test: we want to see how you handle your own numbers being challenged.)
Why does an MSME choose you over Infinite Uptime or Kirloskar's KirloSmart, and have you lost a pilot to either?
what_would_change_our_view: Reconciled subscription revenue showing paying customers renew and add sensors, plus measured alert accuracy across motor types and a named certification path with a timeline.
